title: The effect of changing constituents on tensile mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr high entropy alloy: A molecular dynamics study.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy modeled as a 10–20 nm cubic single crystal with periodic boundaries.
recollection.intervention: Guess: Series of molecular-dynamics tensile tests in which one element at a time was removed or its concentration systematically varied (e.g., 20–0 at %) while temperature was held at 300 K.
recollection.structure: Guess: Body-centred-cubic solid-solution before loading; after deformation, dislocation networks, stacking faults and localized shear bands formed.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Changes in elemental mix altered local lattice distortion and elastic modulus, which in turn changed dislocation nucleation stress and the propensity for twinning; solid-solution strengthening dominated, with larger atomic-size mismatch (Hf, Zr) giving higher strength but lower ductility.
recollection.results: Guess: Ultimate tensile strength ranged from ~2.5 GPa (full equiatomic) to ~1.6 GPa when Zr was removed; yield strain ~3–4 %, fracture strain up to 15 % in Zr-rich compositions; elastic modulus varied from 130 to 180 GPa; strength scaled roughly linearly with the calculated misfit parameter δ.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies MD tensile testing with one constituent varied at a time, including removal, and the main 300 K condition, though it misses the 0–30 at.% design, Hf compensation, and high-temperature tests. It correctly recalls the initial BCC solid solution and shear localization, but adds unsupported stacking faults and dislocation-network details. Solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion are relevant, but the proposed twinning and claim that Hf/Zr mismatch increases strength are unsupported or inconsistent with the paper. Nearly all numerical results and claimed trends are incorrect.
